archive.title: Finite recurrence estimate
archive.body: Write B=V1, C=U1, D=V2 and A=U2. For ordered endpoints with A>=4B, this method additionally requires eta=B(D-C)/(CD)<=1/512. Under its other stated independent hypotheses it proves the comparison estimate. Failure of this sufficient smallness bound does not refute the comparison estimate itself.

archive.title: Two-column energy certificate
archive.body: Let nu be a finite positive measure on [a,b], 0<a<b. Put m_j=integral x^j dnu(x). For every k>=0, the tables (m_(i+j))_(i,j=0..k) and (m_(i+j+1))_(i,j=0..k) are positive semidefinite: their quadratic forms are integral (sum c_i x^i)^2 dnu and integral x(sum c_i x^i)^2 dnu. They are positive definite if the support contains at least k+1 distinct points. With q support points their rank is at most q. In particular m_j*m_(j+2)-m_(j+1)^2>=0 for j>=0. No uniform positive lower eigenvalue follows without quantitative support/weight margins.

archive.title: Adjacent-row certificate
archive.body: An old unresolved construction needs all finite Hankel and shifted Hankel tables of its supplied sequence to be positive semidefinite. The dependency is a positive measure with support on the positive half-line, together with an exact moment identity for every required index. A title, three checked minors, or a limiting approximation cannot close this interface.

archive.title: Exponential average ratio shortcut
archive.body: For a signed exponential mixture, convexity and moment-table positivity are NOT automatic. The expression exp(tz) and compact support alone do not supply a positive measure. This result is only an exclusion of the unsigned-to-signed shortcut.

archive.title: Positive exponential average diagonal
archive.body: If A(z)=exp(cz) for one real c, the associated moment table has rank one. This singleton-support lemma does not establish strict positivity of larger determinants for a general average.

archive.body: For a finite positive measure nu on a positive compact interval and m_j=integral x^j dnu, the Hankel and shifted Hankel tables are positive semidefinite by their polynomial-square quadratic forms. The positivity of nu is indispensable. This theorem says nothing about signed measures.

archive.body: The consumer requires all finite Hankel tables of its supplied sequence to be positive semidefinite. An exact moment identity and positive representing measure would suffice. archive.title: Exponential compact-support sign
archive.body: A finite signed exponential sum has an exact compactly supported signed representation. Compactness does not imply positive weights or convexity.

archive.title: Order-range comparison
archive.body: The comparison is licensed only when the exact bound |r_(s,n)|<=1/8 is available, alongside independently retained hypotheses. This branch asks for an increasing-order range, not merely fixed-order eventual convergence.

archive.title: Order-two bound
archive.body: For s=2 and all integers n>=1, |r_(2,n)|<=1/n. This quantitative estimate is stronger than the general 2^s/n bound at s=2 and remains separately useful.
